newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court denies Rao protection against arrest.
newsitem.headline: Indian court denies Rao protection against arrest.

text.p: An Indian court on Thursday rejected a request by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao for legal protection against arrest in a criminal conspiracy case, court officials said.
The Delhi High court denied Rao's request for anticipatory bail in the $100,000 case, they said. Anticipatory bail protects an accused against arrest.
"The application for anticipatory bail is dismissed," judge S.K. Mahajan said. "The application is not maintainable."
Rao's lawyer had asked on Wednesday for anticipatory bail before a hearing next Monday in the cheating case.
Rao abruptly resigned as president of the Congress party on Saturday after a judge ordered him to appear in court as a co-accused at Monday's hearing.
Indian expatriate businessman Lakhubhai Pathak alleges that Rao and a Hindu guru conspired to cheat him of $100,000 in 1983.

Pathak says he paid the money to guru Chandraswami in an unsuccessful attempt to win a state newsprint contract after Rao, then foreign minister, assured him at a meeting in a New York hotel that his "work would be done."
Rao has said he is innocent and has denied he was in New York on the dates mentioned by Pathak.

The two other accused, Chandraswami and his personal aide, are currently in judicial custody in Tihar jail, Asia's biggest prison, in the Indian capital. Under judicial custody, an accused is detained during an investigation or trial.
Authorities said that at Monday's hearing, the court was expected to bring formal charges of criminal conspiracy against Rao. The charges carry a maximum penalty of seven years in jail.

When Rao resigned as head of Congress, he had already been under pressure to quit after leading India's oldest party to its worst defeat in general elections that ended in May. Congress has ruled India for all but four years since independence from Britain in 1947.
Although a former prime minister and current member of parliament, Rao has no immunity in the case.
Rao's counsel argued on Thursday that his client was bound to be arrested next week because he would be charged with a criminal offence.
"Mr Rao has to be arrested on September 30 when he appears before the trial court, and he has to apply for bail," Rao's lawyer, Kapil Sibal, said.

Arguing against Rao's request for anticipatory bail, the counsel for the Central Bureau of Investigation said the former prime minister was not going to be arrested before September 30, and thus had no reason to ask for anticipatory bail.
Judge Mahajan said no arrest warrant had been issued and, if Rao was detained on Monday, he could immediately ask for ordinary bail.
Court officials said Rao was expected to lodge an appeal of the High Court's decision with the Supreme Court either on Thursday or Friday.
The Times of India newspaper said the government was drawing up a plan for giving Rao medical assistance if he is sent to jail. Rao has a history of heart trouble.
